variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Use 'var' for mutable variables and 'let' for constants. Swift is statically typed but uses type inference.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
let intVal: Int = 42
let floatVal: Float = 3.14
let doubleVal: Double = 3.14159
let boolVal: Bool = true
let stringVal: String = "Swift"
let optionalInt: Int? = nil
data_types.notes: Swift places strong emphasis on safety with optionals (?) representing a value or the absence of a value (nil).

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: Standard operators apply. The nil-coalescing operator (??) unwraps an optional safely or provides a default value.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Parentheses are not required around conditions. 'guard' is used extensively for early returns and safe optional unwrapping.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: Swift uses ranges (... and ..<) for iteration. The C-style for loop is no longer supported.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: 'repeat-while' guarantees that the block executes at least once, akin to 'do-while' in other languages.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Functions can define argument labels (like 'to') and parameter names. Closures provide concise inline function expressions.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.code:
var arr: [Int] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
arr.append(6)

let first = arr[0]
let count = arr.count
arrays.notes: Arrays are value types (structs) in Swift. Using 'let' makes the array immutable.

maps.title: Maps
maps.notes: Dictionaries (maps) are strongly typed. Accessing a dictionary returns an optional value, handled safely via optional binding.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Swift uses do-try-catch blocks for error handling. Functions that can throw errors must be marked with 'throws'.

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.notes: Swift uses C-style // single-line and /* */ multi-line comments.

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Swift provides explicitly sized integer and floating-point primitives with binary and hex support.

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.notes: Swift uses bool / boolean types with true and false literals and logical operators (&&, ||, !).

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Conversion
type_casting.notes: Swift supports explicit type casting using cast operators or constructor functions.

strings.title: Strings & Characters
strings.notes: Swift distinguishes between single-character literals and string sequences or pointer slices.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.code:
let name = "Alice"
let score = 95
let msg = "User \(name) scored \(score)"
string_formatting.notes: Swift supports string interpolation or printf-style formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching & Switch
pattern_matching.code:
switch val {
case 1:
    print("One")
case 2...3:
    print("Two or Three")
default:
    print("Other")
}
pattern_matching.notes: Swift evaluates branching conditions through switch statements, match expressions, or when constructs.

range.title: Ranges & Slicing
range.code:
let r = 1..<5
for i in r { print(i) }
range.notes: Swift represents ranges with range operators (.., ..<) or standard indexed iteration boundaries.

iterators.title: Iterators & Sequences
iterators.notes: Swift implements iteration through Iterator interfaces, generators, or range-for loops.

oop_classes.title: Classes & OOP
oop_classes.notes: Swift models object orientation through classes with constructors/encapsulation or structs with associated methods.

lists.title: Dynamic Arrays & Lists
lists.notes: Swift manages growable dynamic collections using vectors, ArrayLists, or dynamically reallocated heap buffers.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Swift represents heterogeneous records through tuples, structured bindings, or lightweight record structs.

sets.title: Sets & Unique Collections
sets.notes: Swift provides unique collection hashing structures with O(1) average lookup and insertion time.

modules_import.title: Modules, Packages & Imports
modules_import.notes: Swift structures namespaces and external libraries via include directives, package declarations, or module imports.
